Premier says he owns a gun and would not hesitate to use it on someone trying to break into his home
· Posted: Nov 26, 2026 2:14 PM EST | Last Updated: 15 minutes ago
Ontario Premier Doug Ford says he wants to see legal changes to address a spate of home invasions, and in the meantime he is advising people to "use anything you can to protect your family."
Ford says he owns a gun and wouldn't hesitate to use it on someone trying to break into his home, advising people without guns to use knives or baseball bats to protect themselves and their children.

The premier was reacting to the fatal shooting of a 39-year-old musician during an overnight home invasion in an affluent Toronto neighbourhood on Wednesday, which came not long after a violent home invasion in a wealthy part of the city left a family of four injured.

blocks.text: He says he is directing his attorney general and solicitor general to look at legal changes that could bring the province "right up to the edge" of so-called castle law.

Ford has previously mused about introducing the castle doctrine, laws in some U.S. states that allow people to use reasonable force, sometimes including lethal force, to protect themselves in their homes.
Attorney General Doug Downey says there are already rules around self defence, but that they will examine whether the line is in the right spot.
